blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Leading a multicultural British team means balancing two things: the British default of calm, indirect communication, and the reality that your team members may come from cultures where direct, open debate is the norm. A good leader translates between these worlds without asking anyone to become someone they are not.

Practical habits help. Check in with everyone, one to one, in the first months. Make space for different communication styles — some people thrive in open debate, while others need to share their views in writing afterwards. Use "we" and "all of us" rather than "you" and "them".

Over time, the best multicultural teams build a new, hybrid culture: more direct than a traditional British team, more patient than many international ones — and stronger than either.

items.q: According to the text, what does a good leader do when the team mixes different communication styles?
options: Translates between the styles without changing who people are
Asks everyone to adopt the British style
items.why: "A good leader translates between these worlds without asking anyone to become someone they are not."

items.q: Which practical habit does the text recommend for the first months?
options: Checking in one to one with everyone
items.why: "Check in with everyone, one to one, in the first months."

items.q: According to the text, a hybrid multicultural culture is…
options: identical to a traditional British team
more direct and more patient than either side alone
items.why: "more direct than a traditional British team, more patient than many international ones — and stronger than either."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Everyone on the team should be forced to debate openly.
Inclusive language helps a mixed team work together.
Written feedback is a valid way to share views.
Different communication styles can coexist on one team.
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende dar espaço a estilos diferentes — forçar todos ao debate aberto contraria a ideia central.

items.q: The preference for "we" and "all of us" over "you" and "them" suggests that the author values…
options: a sense of shared belonging on the team
items.why: Inferência: linguagem inclusiva sinaliza pertencimento — o time como um só grupo, não lados opostos.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando a nova líder de equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, you've got eight nationalities on this project, and that's a real strength — but only if you manage it well. Let me give you a few things that worked for me.

First, don't assume everyone reads a quiet meeting the same way. For a British colleague, silence might mean polite agreement. For someone used to open debate, that same silence can feel like the room isn't engaged. Your job is to translate between those two habits, not to pick a winner.

Second, book short one-to-one calls with each person in the first few weeks. Ask them plainly how they like to give feedback. Some will happily challenge you in the meeting; others would rather send you their thoughts in writing an hour later. Both are fine — just make space for both.

And watch your words. When you say "you need to fix this," it can sound like blame. When you say "how do we solve this together," the whole team leans in. Use "we" and "all of us." Over time you're not copying the British way or anyone else's — you're building a third culture that's stronger than either.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Sophie, how might a British colleague read silence in a meeting?
items.why: "For a British colleague, silence might mean polite agreement."

items.q: What does Sophie recommend doing in the first few weeks?
options: Booking short one-to-one calls with each person
Sending a written survey to the whole team
items.why: "book short one-to-one calls with each person in the first few weeks."

items.q: How does Sophie feel about people who prefer to send feedback in writing after a meeting?
options: She thinks it should be discouraged
She treats it as equally valid
She prefers it to open debate
She sees it as a lack of commitment
items.why: "Both are fine — just make space for both."

items.q: Why does Sophie suggest saying "how do we solve this together" instead of "you need to fix this"?
options: It avoids sounding like blame and brings the team in
It is shorter and quicker to say
It matches the British style exactly
items.why: Inferência: ela contrasta a linguagem que soa como culpa com a que engaja o time — o foco é o efeito no grupo.

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "building a third culture"?
options: Creating a new shared style that isn't a copy of either side
Making everyone adopt the British way
Hiring people from a third country
Keeping each nationality's habits fully separate
items.why: Inferência: 'terceira cultura' é a mistura híbrida — nem britânica pura nem estrangeira pura, mas algo novo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "She leads a multicultural team spread across five countries." Multicultural means…
options: made up of people from many cultures
items.why: Multicultural = multicultural: composto por pessoas de várias culturas.

items.q: "For many British staff, indirect feedback is the default." A default is…
options: the standard, automatic way something is done
items.why: Default = padrão: o modo automático, o que acontece por hábito.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Some colleagues prefer open ___, challenging ideas out loud in the meeting."
items.why: Open debate = debate aberto: discutir e desafiar ideias em voz alta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The team ended up with a ___ culture — part British, part international — and it worked better than either."
items.why: Hybrid = híbrido: mistura de dois estilos, que foi o que o time construiu.

items.q: "A good leader uses inclusive language so no one feels like an outsider." Inclusive language…
options: makes everyone feel part of the group
items.why: Inclusive = inclusivo: linguagem que faz todos se sentirem parte do grupo (ex.: 'we', 'all of us').

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem ao liderar equipes multiculturais. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "I try to check in with each new joiner every week." To check in with someone means to…
options: briefly touch base to see how they are doing
items.why: Check in with = dar um alô, ver como a pessoa está, sem formalidade.

items.q: "A couple of colleagues pushed back on the new schedule." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Let's make space for people who prefer to speak up later." To make space for something means to…
items.why: Make space for = abrir espaço, permitir deliberadamente que algo aconteça.

items.q: "Great — we agreed a plan, now we just need to follow through." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "When she said 'how do we solve this,' the whole team started to lean in." To lean in means to…
options: engage more actively and get involved
items.why: Lean in = engajar-se, entrar de cabeça na conversa ou no problema.
